article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 80% Indica / 20% Sativa
Genetics: Warlock × Rockstar
Breeder: DNA Genetics
THC Content: 18–25%
CBD Content: Typically below 1%
Terpene Profile: myrcene , beta-caryophyllene , humulene
Primary Flavors: Sweet fruit, berries, lavender, hash
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: late September through October
Indoor Yield: 500–600 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: 600 g per plant
Grow Difficulty: Easy to moderate

Rocklock belongs to a generation of cannabis strains bred before elaborate dessert names and 30%-THC marketing became the center of the strain market. DNA Genetics gave the cultivar a much simpler assignment: take two heavy, resinous parents, shorten the flowering cycle, keep the plant manageable, and produce enough dense marijuana to satisfy growers looking for an uncomplicated indica. Warlock and Rockstar supplied the raw material, while the finished hybrid delivered broad leaves, thick lateral growth, crystal-coated flowers, and a bloom measured in roughly eight weeks. Historical DNA Genetics catalog material described Rocklock as one of the company’s original strains and emphasized high-density planting, large buds, heavy resin production, and minimal maintenance.

What makes the strain more interesting than a straightforward couch-lock plant is the contrast after harvest. Its buds can smell sweet and fruity before opening into hash, lavender, spice, and earthy herbs. The high develops along a similar line: a heavy body sensation may build quickly, yet the mind can remain surprisingly awake and engaged. That combination gave Rocklock a personality distinct from the purely sedative marijuana hybrids that its 80% indica classification might suggest.
Genetics and Lineage

The original DNA Genetics formula is Warlock × Rockstar. Archived G.Y.O. listings preserve that exact lineage along with the breeder’s 80% indica / 20% sativa classification, eight-week flowering cycle, and 500–600 g/m² indoor yield. Contemporary archives of the DNA catalog provide the same specifications, making the parental combination unusually well documented for an older cultivar that is no longer prominent in the company’s current lineup.

Warlock contributes an established old-school indica foundation with enough cerebral character to keep the finished hybrid from feeling one-dimensional. Rockstar reinforces density, resin, earthy pungency, and a heavier physical side. Together, the parents produced a short-to-medium plant with substantial branching and unusually compact flowers. Rather than chasing exotic color or a single extreme terpene note, DNA Genetics selected around practical indoor traits: speed, flower weight, resin coverage, and ease of cultivation.

Rocklock was eventually offered through DNA Genetics’ G.Y.O. Collection, a lower-cost line built around established genetics from the breeder’s own library and selected outside material. Historical descriptions repeatedly call it one of DNA’s earlier creations and present it as a production-oriented indica suitable even for less-experienced growers. That background helps explain why the strain is remembered as much for its garden performance as for its effects.
Effects and Experience

Rocklock’s first impression can be misleading. The body may begin to feel warm and weighted fairly quickly, creating the unmistakable physical pressure expected from a strongly indica-dominant hybrid. Muscles loosen, movement becomes less urgent, and a comfortable seated position can become increasingly attractive. DNA’s old marketing leaned heavily into this characteristic, effectively presenting the cultivar as a plant designed to put the “lock” into couch-lock.

The mind, however, does not always follow the body immediately. Moderate amounts can retain an alert, imaginative quality while physical relaxation continues building underneath. That makes the experience somewhat unusual: rather than simply becoming sleepy, a consumer may feel heavy yet mentally interested in music, conversation, movies, or creative thought. Larger servings generally reduce that balance and push the cultivar toward a more conventional evening indica experience.

There is no trustworthy universal THC number for Rocklock. The original breeder literature called the potency high but did not publish a laboratory percentage. Later commercial references have placed flower anywhere from the upper teens into the low-to-mid 20% range, illustrating why a single figure should not be treated as a genetic constant. Consumers should use the cannabinoid analysis of the actual product when available, particularly because excessive THC can produce dry mouth, dizziness, anxiety, impaired coordination, or unwanted sedation.
Medical Benefits

The physical character of Rocklock made it attractive within the older medical marijuana market, especially among consumers who preferred a heavy body sensation without necessarily becoming immediately asleep. Smaller amounts may allow the mental component to remain relatively active while bodily tension begins to soften, whereas larger doses generally emphasize deeper relaxation.

Those historical uses should not be confused with clinical evidence. Rocklock itself has not been demonstrated in controlled trials to treat pain, insomnia, anxiety, muscle spasms, depression, or another condition. The chemical composition of cannabis flower also changes according to phenotype and cultivation. Medical consumers should therefore base decisions on tested cannabinoid content, dosage, personal tolerance, medication interactions, and appropriate healthcare guidance rather than strain reputation alone.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Rocklock occupies an older aromatic territory than today’s candy-heavy weed. Sweet fruit can be immediately noticeable, but it is usually surrounded by earthy herbs, hash, spice, and a faint floral quality. Berry and lavender notes may emerge in better-cured examples, creating a profile that feels softer and more complex than the harsh Skunk aroma its dense indica appearance might imply.

No standardized terpene analysis from DNA Genetics has been preserved for the original strain. Modern descriptions most frequently associate the cultivar with myrcene, beta-caryophyllene, and humulene, but those should be treated as commonly observed terpenes rather than a fixed breeder specification. Myrcene fits the earthy, musky fruit character, caryophyllene reinforces dry pepper and spice, and humulene contributes woody, herbal depth.

During consumption, sweetness tends to become more apparent than it is in the jar. Berry and fruit notes can lead the inhale before lavender, herbs, spice, and a distinctly hash-like quality develop through the finish. Some phenotypes may lean more citrusy, while others emphasize musk and earth. Proper curing matters because the lighter floral and fruit notes disappear quickly when the flower becomes excessively dry.
Growing Information

Cultivation was central to Rocklock’s original appeal. DNA Genetics described the plant as suitable for high-density growing, capable of producing large crystal-coated flowers with relatively little attention. Archived breeder listings give an indoor flowering period of eight weeks and a yield of approximately 500–600 g/m². The breeder also promoted the cultivar as a good option for newer growers because its compact indica structure and short bloom reduced some of the management required by taller or slower varieties.

Plants typically remain short to medium in height while developing broad leaves and strong side branches. That architecture makes Rocklock compatible with closely packed indoor gardens and Sea-of-Green-style production. Individual plants can also be topped or trained to spread their lateral growth more evenly beneath the light. As flowering progresses, the dense buds accumulate enough resin and weight that airflow becomes increasingly important.

Historical retail material lists indoor production consistently around 500–600 g/m², while older outdoor references have placed favorable plants near 600 g each. Outdoor maturity is generally associated with late September through October, depending on climate and latitude. Because the flowers become compact, growers in wet autumn environments need to watch humidity carefully as harvest approaches. Rocklock’s strongest horticultural advantage remains straightforward efficiency: a relatively quick crop, substantial flower density, and respectable production without requiring an especially complex plant-management strategy.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Rocklock?
Rocklock is Warlock × Rockstar, bred by DNA Genetics. Archived DNA G.Y.O. catalog material lists the cultivar as an 80% indica / 20% sativa hybrid.
Is Rocklock indica or sativa?

DNA Genetics classified Rocklock as approximately 80% indica and 20% sativa. Its growth is strongly indica-like, although the effects can retain more cerebral stimulation than its genetics might initially suggest.
How strong is Rocklock?

The original breeder described Rocklock as potent but did not publish a standardized THC percentage. Later examples are commonly estimated somewhere around 18–25% THC. Batch-specific laboratory testing is therefore more reliable than assigning one permanent potency figure.
What does Rocklock taste like?
Sweet fruit and berries combine with lavender, earthy herbs, hash, and spice. Some plants may also develop mild citrus or musky characteristics depending on phenotype and cultivation.
How long does Rocklock take to flower?
DNA Genetics’ historical specifications list an indoor flowering period of approximately eight weeks, with yields around 500–600 g/m².
Final Thoughts on Rocklock

Rocklock reflects a practical school of marijuana breeding that deserves more attention than it usually receives. DNA Genetics was not trying to create the most colorful flower or invent a new candy flavor. Warlock and Rockstar were combined to build a compact, heavily resinous indica capable of producing large yields in roughly eight weeks without demanding constant intervention from the grower. Archived DNA material consistently preserves the same essential profile: 80% indica, large crystal-covered buds, strong resin production, and about 500–600 g/m² indoors.

Its character after harvest prevents that agricultural efficiency from becoming boring. Fruit, berries, lavender, hash, earth, and spice give Rocklock more aromatic range than a generic production indica, while the high combines substantial body relaxation with an unexpectedly awake cerebral component at moderate doses. For cannabis enthusiasts exploring older DNA Genetics releases, Rocklock remains a good example of the breeder’s early approach: straightforward genetics, short flowering, practical yields, and enough personality to keep the weed interesting long after the original seed release disappeared from most modern catalogs.
